svg.text: Two independent services · OAuth2-style RS256 / JWKS cross-service auth · async end-to-end · zero auth hop on the hot path
Docker Compose — bridge network · healthchecks · ordered startup (depends_on)
Auth provider · token issuer · FastAPI on :8001
users — UUID PK · unique email · role enum · Argon2 hash
Alembic migrations on startup · asyncpg pool · pool_pre_ping
Resource server · stateless — no database · FastAPI on :8002
Local RS256 verification — no network on the hot path
JWKS cached by kid · validates iss · aud · exp · 401 / 403 + WWW-Authenticate
Segmented Sieve of Eratosthenes — base primes ≤ √end + 64 KB windows
Memory stays flat at ANY range size · end ≤ 10⁸ cap (DoS guard → 422)
Runs in threadpool → the event loop never blocks
asyncio.gather — 3 upstreams in parallel · latency ≈ slowest source
Each source isolated: timeout / 4xx / 5xx / parse → its own status
Always HTTP 200 with a unified envelope → graceful partial success
INTERNET — keyless public APIs · no secrets
call protected APIs — Authorization: Bearer <access token> · validated locally, no hop to Identity
5 s timeout · failures isolated per source
TASK B UNIFIED RESPONSE — always HTTP 200
register / log in → access JWT (15 min) + refresh (7 d)
Bearer token → Client verifies signature locally
JWKS fetched once · re-fetch only on unknown kid
RS256 asymmetric — private key never leaves Identity
Resource servers verify via public JWKS → no shared secrets
Argon2id + dummy-verify ⇒ constant-time login, no enumeration
Refresh: SHA-256 at rest · rotation · reuse ⇒ family revoked
RBAC require_role · UUID PKs · generic 401s · env-only config
Docker: healthchecks · depends_on ordering · non-root images
Poetry-locked deps · Alembic migrations · fail-fast .env config
FastAPI Developer Technical Assessment · Hassaan Ali · June 2026
